facts.fact: The Ministry of Economy and Finance has rolled out the BADR system for customs clearance, and the customs IT system is integrated with key partners in the foreign trade chain, per the budget minister.
ADII and ANP say the electronic delivery order (BAD), dematerialised in 2020, is exchanged among port actors over PortNet, the Guichet Unique du Commerce Extérieur platform.
ADII says detailed declarations are registered on its BADR system, which sends data automatically to the industry ministry through PortNet, now at all import clearance offices.
ADII says the PortNet foreign-trade single window carries ministry authorisations and conformity-check results to customs by EDI, generalised to all import offices.
Moroccan Customs says declarations have been lodged by computer since 1991 and clearance entered total dematerialisation in 2019, on the online clearance system BADR.
PortNet's monthly report says it processed 191,388 Single Goods Declarations (DUM) in June 2026, 115,180 import and 76,208 export declarations.
The 7News report describes PortNet as Morocco's National Single Window for Foreign Trade, connecting customs, ports, banks and businesses, with 95,753 active users in June 2026.
Express TV reports that the BADR system is the backbone of Morocco's digital customs transactions, with an audit begun in January 2025.

Morocco's customs directorate launched international tender No. 6/2026, about MAD 7.2 million, to carry out the BADR audit recommendations and move it to a cloud-native microservices architecture, with bids opening 16 April 2026.

facts.fact: The ADII 2024 activity report says the number of customs declarations rose 7.1% to pass two million for the first time, processed through its BADR system.
